;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[2019 India–Pakistan standoff]]
**The [[Pakistani Air Force]] claims it has carried out [[2019 Jammu and Kashmir airstrikes|six airstrikes]] in Indian-administered [[Jammu and Kashmir (state)|Jammu and Kashmir]], shooting down one Indian aircraft and capturing one pilot following a [[dogfight]]. Pakistani officials claimed that they have shot down two Indian Air Force (IAF) jets. Wreckage of one aircraft fell in [[Azad Kashmir]] while the other fell in Indian-administered Kashmir. Indian officials initially rejected that any of their aircraft was shot down and claimed that all of IAF pilots were accounted for. However, later on they acknowledge that one IAF Mig-21 has been shot down and its pilot was captured by the Pakistan Army. India officials also claimed to have shot down one Pakistani Air Force (PAF) jet that violated its airspace. However, Indian officials claim were rejected by Pakistani officials. [https://www.theweek.in/news/india/2019/02/27/pakistan-jets-violate-indian-air-space-kashmir-nowshera-drop-bombs.html (''The Week (India)'')] [https://mobile.twitter.com/ndtv/status/1100656090805686272 (NDTV)][https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/news/pakistan-violates-indian-air-space-in-nowshera/article26383265.ece (''The Hindu Business Line'')][https://www.dawn.com/news/1466413 (''Dawn News'')]
**An [[Indian Air Force]] [[Mil Mi-17|Mi-17]] [[transport helicopter]] crashes in the [[Budgam district]] of [[Jammu and Kashmir (state)|Jammu and Kashmir]], killing all six IAF personnel onboard and a civilian on the ground. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/military-aircraft-crashes-in-jammu-and-kashmir-s-budgam-district/story-6SPgXbpkV7oc39JHSdM6lM.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
*[[Israeli involvement in the Syrian Civil War]], [[Israel–Russia relations]]
**[[Prime Minister of Israel|Israeli Prime Minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] tells [[President of Russia|Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] that Israel will "continue to take action against Iran in Syria". [https://www.timesofisrael.com/netanyahu-tells-putin-israel-will-continue-to-take-action-against-iran-in-syria/ (''The Times of Israel'')]

;Arts and culture
*[[Ukraine in the Eurovision Song Contest 2019]]
**[[Ukraine]] withdraws from this year's [[Eurovision Song Contest 2019|Eurovision Song Contest]] in [[Tel Aviv]], [[Israel]], after Ukrainian entrant [[Maruv]] said she refused to be used as a "political tool" after being asked to sign a contract saying she wouldn't hold any concerts in [[Russia]] in the lead up to the event. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/entertainment-arts-47394371 (BBC News)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[Ramses Station train collision]]
**A train crash and subsequent fire kills at least 25 people at [[Ramses Station]] in [[Cairo]], [[Egypt]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-47384443 (BBC News)]
**Egyptian Transport Minister [[Hisham Arafat]] consequently resigns. [[Prime Minister of Egypt|Prime Minister]] [[Mostafa Madbouly]] accepts the resignation. [http://www.africanews.com/2019/02/27/egypt-at-least-25-killed-as-train-crashes-at-cairo-station/ (Africa News)]
*[[2019 Taplejung helicopter crash]]
**A helicopter crashes in [[Taplejung]], [[Nepal]], killing 7 people, including Nepal's culture and tourism minister [[Rabindra Prasad Adhikari]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/02/27/world/asia/nepal-helicopter-crash-tourism-minister.html (''The New York Times'')]
*A suspected gas explosion in [[Taraz]], [[Kazakhstan]], kills three people in an apartment block. [https://www.rferl.org/a/explosion-kills-three-partially-destroys-residential-building-in-kazakhstan/29793630.html (RFERL)]
*[[list of disasters in Indonesia|Disasters in Indonesia]]
**A landslide hits an illegal gold mine in [[North Sulawesi]], [[Sulawesi]], [[Indonesia]]. An estimated 60 people are trapped underground as shafts give way, while three others are found dead. [https://news.sky.com/story/at-least-three-dead-and-dozens-buried-alive-in-indonesia-gold-mine-collapse-11649457 (Sky News)]

;International relations
*[[2019 North Korea–United States Hanoi Summit]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] and [[List of leaders of North Korea|North Korean leader]] [[Kim Jong-un]] meet face-to-face for the first time since their [[2018 North Korea-United States Singapore Summit|summit]] last year. [https://www.cnbc.com/2019/02/27/trump-and-kim-meet-face-to-face-in-vietnam-as-second-summit-kicks-off.html (CNBC)]
*[[Brexit negotiations]]
**[[Member of Parliament (United Kingdom)|MPs]] in the [[House of Commons]] meet to discuss [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|UK Prime Minister]] [[Theresa May]]'s latest proposed deal for the state's departure from the [[European Union]]. May says if this proposal and a 'no deal' scenario are both rejected by MPs they will be granted a vote on extending the departure deadline beyond the current one of March 29. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-politics-47380314 (BBC News)]
**[[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative]] MP [[Alberto Costa (British politician)|Alberto Costa]] tables an amendment to secure the rights of EU citizens within the UK and UK citizens abroad. Theresa May tells Commons she opposes the amendment; [[Home Secretary]] [[Sajid Javid]] subsequently supports it, apparently unaware of May's opposition. Costa resigns as parliamentary private secretary to [[Secretary of State for Scotland|Scottish Secretary]] [[David Mundell]], who supports the amendment. The government subsequently announces it will support the amendment. [https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2019/feb/27/confusion-reigns-over-brexit-amendment-as-tory-mp-alberto-costa-sacked (''The Guardian'')]
;Law and crime
*[[Timeline of investigations into Donald Trump and Russia (2019)]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]]'s former attorney, [[Michael Cohen (lawyer)|Michael Cohen]], is prepared to testify that Trump was aware of longtime adviser [[Roger Stone]]'s efforts to make contact with [[WikiLeaks]] in advance of its release of damaging information about [[Hillary Clinton 2016 presidential campaign|Hillary Clinton's 2016 presidential campaign]], according to a copy of his public testimony submitted to Congress and obtained by CNN. [https://www.cnn.com/2019/02/27/politics/michael-cohen-testimony/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Child sexual abuse in the United Kingdom]]
**Nine men receive prison terms for raping two vulnerable teenage girls in [[Bradford]] over a period of years. A tenth is cleared. The abuse began when the victims were fourteen. The girls were from a children's home. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-leeds-47388060 (BBC News)]
*[[Human rights in Israel]], [[Timeline of the Israeli–Palestinian conflict|Terrorism in Israel]]
**[[Shin Bet]] arrest lawyer Tarek Barghout, an attorney who has represented "terror" suspects, and a [[Palestinian people|Palestinian man]] named Zakaria Zubeidi for what it calls "their involvement in serious and current terrorist activities." [https://www.timesofisrael.com/israel-arrests-former-terrorist-leader-citing-serious-current-activities/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
*[[Steven Avery]], a high-profile [[miscarriage of justice]] victim subsequently convicted of murder after his release in 2003, is granted a fresh appeal in [[Wisconsin]]. Avery, who was suing [[Manitowoc County]] officials over his original wrongful conviction when he was arrested for murder, gained international attention as the subject of the documentary ''[[Making a Murderer]]''. [https://news.sky.com/story/making-a-murderers-steven-avery-is-granted-an-appeal-against-murder-conviction-11649607 (Sky News)]
*The family of [[Pat Finucane]], murdered during [[The Troubles]] in [[Northern Ireland]], win a declaration from the [[uK Supreme Court|Supreme Court of the United Kingdom]] that the investigation into his killing was sufficiently ineffective to amount to a failure of the state's obligations under the [[European Convention on Human Rights]]. The Supreme Court stops short of mandating a [[public inquiry]] as requested by the family. Members of the security services are accepted to have colluded with Finucane's murderers, but the scale and nature of collusion is unclear. [https://news.sky.com/story/family-lose-legal-bid-to-force-public-inquiry-into-pat-finucane-murder-11649740 (Sky News)]
;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Venezuelan presidential crisis]]
**[[Juan Guaidó]] announces that he will exercise his "duties as president" when he returns to Venezuela from Colombia. Guaidó also stated that he did not see any signs of "broad support" from Russia towards [[Nicolás Maduro]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2019/02/27/us/venezuela-guaido-presidential-duties/index.html (CNN)], [https://www.forbes.com/sites/kenrapoza/2019/02/27/venezuelas-guaido-says-russia-not-propping-up-nicolas-maduro/#34d3ba656b91 (''Forbes'')]
**[[Colombia]] asks for intervention from the [[United Nations]] to help end the crisis. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-venezuela-politics-colombia-un/colombia-calls-at-un-for-action-on-venezuela-crisis-idUSKCN1QG1FU (Reuters)]
*[[Antisemitism in the UK Labour Party]]
**[[Chris Williamson (politician)|Chris Williamson]], a [[UK Labour Party|Labour]] MP, is suspended by his party over comments that Labour had "given too much ground" when responding to criticism over its handling of [[antisemitism]] within its ranks. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-politics-47393626 (BBC News)]
